title: Re: Show HN: Web2MD – turn any URL into clean Markdown...
text:
I built this because my MCP clients kept needing web content as clean text for RAG and research — most URL tools return raw HTML or dump the whole page.

How it works: - Free API: http://167.233.135.161:9999/api/convert?url=... (10/day, no signup). Strips nav, ads, boilerplate. - MCP server (stdio + streamable HTTP): one tool, web2md_convert. Works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Continue.dev, Windsurf. Published in the official MCP registry (io.github.astra-intelligence/web2md). - CLI + Dockerfile in the repo.

Honest scope: single-page conversion today (no site crawls, no PDFs yet). Feedback welcome — especially on output quality vs. readability, and whether people want batch/crawl next.

The repo: https://github.com/astra-intelligence/web2md-mcp

title: Re: Gemini ending free use of Flash and Pro models...
text:
Flash and Pro models are moving to paid plans, free users will only get Flash-Lite. Flash-Lite is the same model used by the Android phone Gemini app and AI Overviews in Google Search, which is very poor at reasoning and makes many errors.

Personally, I've been using the free plan quite a lot and never hit a rate limit, but noticed the quality dropping. Pro was almost never available. Perhaps they aren't able to deliver a good quality Flash model to free users.

title: Re: Memory-Safe WebP Decoding...
text:
As part of Google's PR for their upcoming Gemini 4 Argon LLM release they said they'd rewritten a few things in rust replacing hand written simd. But I don't think webp was mentioned.

They said:

> Large Scale Codebase Migrations and Optimizations: Argon agents are working on migrating C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google — scaling from tens of thousands of lines in core libraries like re2, libgav1 up to 800K+ lines for the Fuchsia Zircon kernel. Given the criticality of many of these systems, such large-scale rewrites are undergoing rigorous automated and manual auditing, emulation testing, and review before rolling out to production.

> For libgav1, Google's open source software for decoding video, Argon agents took an existing Rust port and replaced 32K lines of SIMD code by running many rounds of profile-guided experiments, studying the compiler's output, producing safe Rust so the compiler would vectorize it automatically. The end result is a memory-safe video decoder that runs 2.7x faster than the Rust port, with identical video output, bringing it closer to the optimized C++.
